title: Define demo scenarios + success criteria for Standard Demo v1 (known-good matrix)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Define 4–6 “known-good” demo scenarios for the Standard Demo v1, including owners, required artifacts (scripts, prompt sets, expected outputs, Console clickpaths, dashboards), and measurable success criteria. Output becomes the source for:
- Demo Day dry runs
- Talk track branches (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Regression checks + reset checklist

Context / why
Sales + SE are currently relying on ad-hoc flows. We need a stable demo tenant with repeatable scenarios that show Redwood differentiators without flakiness, sensitive data, or improvised steps.

Principles
- Each scenario must be runnable in <5 minutes (excluding optional deep dive).
- Every scenario must have Plan B (fallback path if live output varies or a Console panel is slow).
- All inputs must be demo-safe (sanitized) and deterministic-ish (tight prompts + temperature constraints where possible), with “expected output characteristics” (not exact text) to avoid overpromising.
- Each scenario must map to at least one persona: Platform Eng, ML Eng, Security/Compliance, Procurement/IT.

Deliverable
A completed “Known Good Matrix” (scenario list) with:
- Scenario name + short narrative (what it proves)
- Persona relevance
- Required tenant config (route/model/version pinning, quotas, rollouts)
- Assets to produce (curl/SDK script, prompt set, expected output, screenshots/clickpath)
- Console views/dashboards required
- Success criteria + thresholds (reliability, latency/cost proof points, time-to-run)
- Owner(s) + reviewer(s)
- Regression check definition (what to automate / what to verify manually)

Proposed scenarios (v1)
1) “Streaming chat + quickstart” (Hosted-first)
- What it shows: fast onboarding, streaming UX, stable latency with sane defaults.
- Persona: ML Eng, product engineers; good opening for PLG-to-sales prospects.
- Artifacts: curl + SDK script (Node/Python), pre-canned prompt, expected streaming behavior notes (first token time, smooth streaming, truncation handling).
- Success criteria:
  - Runs end-to-end in <= 2 minutes.
  - 0 auth surprises (token + tenant pre-validated).
  - Streaming does not disconnect in standard network conditions.
- Owner: Renee Sullivan (scripts) + Colin O’Donnell (integration).

2) “Structured output / JSON mode (validation + retries)”
- What it shows: production-oriented output constraints, schema validation, fewer downstream failures.
- Persona: ML Eng, app engineers.
- Artifacts: request with schema, expected output characteristics (valid JSON, required fields present), a “bad output” example to explain guardrails.
- Success criteria:
  - Schema pass rate during dry run >= 95% (with demo settings) OR clearly explained automatic retry/repair behavior.
  - Demo script includes a safe narrative for nondeterminism.
- Owner: Simran Kaur (scenario) + Amara Diallo (gateway/validation guidance).

3) “Tool calling (simple function) + tracing hook”
- What it shows: tool calls are reliable and inspectable; Redwood supports app patterns beyond plain chat.
- Persona: ML Eng; also resonates with platform teams evaluating standardized interfaces.
- Artifacts: tool spec + sample tool response, script demonstrating model selecting tool and producing final answer; Console trace/saved view link.
- Success criteria:
  - Tool call occurs within 1–2 turns using canned input.
  - Console view clearly shows tool call payload and token/cost breakdown.
- Owner: Colin O’Donnell (integration) + Chloe Martin (Console view requirements).

4) “Routing + fallback (graceful degradation)” (Dedicated + reliability storyline)
- What it shows: policy routing and automatic fallback when a target route is constrained; production reliability posture.
- Persona: Platform Eng, SRE-adjacent buyers.
- Setup: pinned primary model + compatible fallback variant; pre-configured routing policy; a controlled failure mode (e.g., forced capacity constraint / simulated 5xx on primary route).
- Artifacts: script that triggers fallback and a pre-recorded screenshot/backup clip if live behavior is too risky.
- Success criteria:
  - Demo reliably demonstrates “primary → fallback” within one run.
  - Clear explanation of what triggers fallback and how it’s audited.
- Owner: Mina Haddad (routing) + Sean Gallagher (reliability review) + Markus Klein (field usability).

5) “Cost controls: batching/caching impact + token-level cost dashboard”
- What it shows: Redwood’s unit economics levers are observable; token-level breakdown; before/after narrative.
- Persona: Platform Eng, engineering leadership, procurement (value framing).
- Setup: a fixed prompt set run twice (baseline vs optimized policy); dashboard showing cost/token + latency.
- Artifacts: prompt set + expected metric deltas (ranges), saved dashboard view, narration about trade-offs (latency vs throughput).
- Success criteria:
  - Dashboard updates within acceptable lag for a live demo (define threshold with Logan/Chloe).
  - Numbers shown as relative improvements or safe ranges (no hard pricing).
- Owner: Logan Wright (telemetry) + Chloe Martin (dashboard UX) + Soojin Lee (messaging guardrails).

6) “Private/VPC story + security posture (no live deploy)” (optional / security-first)
- What it shows: deployment flexibility; security controls; isolation; audit logs; KMS/SSO posture.
- Persona: Security/compliance, regulated industries.
- Format: Console screenshots + FAQ-driven Q&A, plus a short “how it works” diagram (no risky live setup).
- Artifacts: slide screenshots + security FAQ references + standard answers (retention/logging, encryption, access control).
- Success criteria:
  - Clear statement of demo tenant sanitization/isolation.
  - Pre-approved wording for SOC2/audit log topics (no overclaims).
- Owner: Naomi Feldman (requirements) + Marcus Lin (security review) + Soojin Lee (talk track).

Open questions (need decisions)
- How many scenarios are required for “v1 complete”? Proposal: 5 required (1–5) + #6 as optional branch for security-heavy calls.
- What’s the acceptable level of nondeterminism in outputs? Proposal: define “expected output characteristics” and always have canned outputs for the deck.
- How to demonstrate fallback without creating real instability? Proposal: a controlled toggle (preferred) OR a pre-recorded fallback clip as Plan B.
- Metrics: do we set explicit p95 targets in internal docs, or keep as “dashboard green + within approved range”? Proposal: internal targets are fine, but deck/talk track should use relative language.

Required artifacts checklist (per scenario)
- [ ] Script (curl and at least one SDK) with exact commands
- [ ] Prompt set / inputs (demo-safe)
- [ ] Expected output characteristics + screenshots if applicable
- [ ] Console clickpath steps (what to click, where to look)
- [ ] Plan B (what to do if output varies / dashboard lags / throttling)
- [ ] Owner + backup owner
- [ ] Regression check definition (automated vs manual)

Acceptance criteria
- Scenario list finalized (4–6) with owners and persona mapping.
- Each scenario has all required artifacts defined (not necessarily implemented in this ticket, but unblocked).
- Success criteria documented for each scenario (time-to-run, reliability, and what constitutes “pass”).
- Known Good Matrix is published and linked from PM-1842 and the demo runbook.

Links / references
- Confluence: Demo environment PRD (to be linked by PM)
- Drive: “Demo Scenarios - Known Good Matrix” (source of truth for scenario table)
- Linear: ENG-4921 (demo scripts), ENG-4922 (dashboards), ENG-4923 (regression check)

Out of scope (for this ticket)
- Building bespoke vertical demos per industry
- Final deck design/polish (tracked in PM-1842 / DES-311)
- Implementing tenant automation and dashboards (tracked in ENG tickets)
comments: 2025-08-06 — Soojin Lee: Strongly agree on keeping outputs as “characteristics” and avoiding exact text commitments. For the deck, we should use screenshots/canned outputs for anything that can vary. Also flag: avoid quoting any $/1M token numbers; keep to relative cost/throughput proof points tied to dashboard views.

2025-08-07 — Markus Klein: From the field: routing/fallback is the #1 differentiator for platform teams, but it’s also where live demos get risky. I’d like an explicit Plan B: a pre-recorded clip + screenshots with timestamps so we can narrate confidently if the live toggle doesn’t behave.

2025-08-08 — Naomi Feldman: For security-first calls, we must lead with (a) demo tenant is sanitized, (b) logging posture, (c) retention defaults and what’s configurable, (d) access controls. Please route any SOC2 wording through PMM + security before it hits the talk track.

2025-08-12 — Logan Wright: Dashboard lag: we can get near-real-time for request traces, but cost panels may have a short delay depending on aggregation window. Suggest success criteria be “panel updates within 60–90s” and have a saved view showing last 15 minutes + a pre-captured screenshot for Plan B.

2025-08-15 — Simran Kaur: Drafted v0.2 of scenarios list with owners + artifacts; need final decision on whether structured output is required or optional. I’m leaning required because it demos production readiness and reduces “LLMs are flaky” objections.
